package: flexible strip, 12 mm wide, 4.6 mm thick, IP65 silicone sheath; 3-pin JST SM connectors at both ends, extra power wires at the input; cut between any two pixels

datasheet.title: Pololu product page: Addressable RGB 60-LED Strip, 5V, 1m (WS2812B), item #2549

hints: WS2812B pixels: the blue and green LEDs need 3.0–3.4 V and 3.0–3.2 V of their own (data sheet, LED characteristic parameter, p. 4) – where the supply along the strip sags, blue and green fade first and the far end turns red (Pololu: 'As the voltage drops, RGB LEDs tend to look redder and draw less current')
Pololu recommends at most 180 LEDs from a single supply and feeding longer chains in sections, with the +5V wires cut between sections fed from different supplies (product page, Chaining)

DIN: VIH ≥ 0.7 × VDD (3.5 V at 5 V) – a 3.3 V MCU needs a level shifter (data sheet p. 3; Pololu: 'The minimum logic high threshold for the strip data line is 3.5 V'); Pololu suggests 100–500 Ω in series with the data line
sources: Pololu product page, Addressable RGB 60-LED Strip, 5V, 1m (WS2812B), item #2549, https://www.pololu.com/product/2549, read 2026-10-31 (discontinued; the page and its measurements still online) – the information applies to all of Pololu's WS2812B strips
pixels_per_m 60: product page, '60 LEDs per meter' (1 m, 60 LEDs; 2 m, 120 LEDs is item #2550)

i_pixel_a 0.05: product page, Features and specifications: 'Each RGB LED draws approximately 50 mA at 5 V with red, green, and blue at full brightness'; the measurement below, 3.0 A for 60 LEDs, gives the same

r_vdd_ohm_per_m 0.2, r_gnd_ohm_per_m 0.2: derived from the product page, Current draw and voltage drop: 'The 60 LED 1 m strip drew 3.0 A and had a voltage drop of 0.6 V', the drop 'computed by measuring the voltage difference between ground and power on the input end of the strip, then doing the same measurement on the output end'. A current drawn evenly along the strip drops I × R × L / 2 between its ends, so both rails together R = 2 × 0.6 V / (3.0 A × 1 m) = 0.40 Ω/m – split evenly between +5V and GND: assumption, the measurement gives only their sum. The 120 LED 2 m strip (4.7 A, 1.4 V) gives 0.30 Ω/m by the same formula: there the far LEDs draw less as the voltage falls, the current is not even and the formula reads low – the 1 m strip, at 0.6 V of drop, is the closer to an even load
Worldsemi WS2812B data sheet (no revision stated; PDF created 2013-10-31), via Pololu https://www.pololu.com/file/0J705/WS2812B_datasheet.pdf, linked from the product page, read 2026-10-31

vdd_op_min_v 3.5, vdd_op_max_v 5.3, pin 5V v_max_v 5.3: data sheet p. 2, Absolute Maximum Ratings, power supply voltage VDD +3.5~+5.3 V – the only supply range the data sheet gives, taken as operating range as well: assumption (as for the WS2812B-V5/W, C2874885); its electrical characteristics hold at VDD 4.5–5.5 V (p. 2–3)
DIN vih_ratio 0.7, vil_ratio 0.3: data sheet p. 3, VIH 0.7 VDD min, VIL 0.3 VDD max (TA −20 … +70 °C, VDD 4.5–5.5 V)
DIN v_rel_max_v 0.5: data sheet p. 2, input voltage VI −0.5 ~ VDD + 0.5 V

pins: product page, Using the LED strip and Cutting – input connector with ground, signal input and power, output connector with ground, signal output and power at the other end; all ground wires joined, all power wires joined; pads labelled 5V, Din, Dout or Do, GND. Pin numbers are the entry's own (no EasyEDA symbol): 1–3 the input end, 4–6 the output end

verified.datasheet: Pololu product page #2549 (read 2026-10-31); Worldsemi WS2812B data sheet (no revision stated, PDF of 2013-10-31) via Pololu
checked: product page: 60 LEDs/m, about 50 mA per LED at full white and 5 V, the five measurements of current and drop, 20 AWG connector wires
data sheet p. 2–4: VDD +3.5~+5.3 V, VI −0.5 ~ VDD + 0.5 V, VIH 0.7 VDD, VIL 0.3 VDD, LED forward voltages
open: the rail resistance is derived from one measurement of Pololu's (even current assumed, +5V and GND rails assumed alike) – a strip of another make has other copper: measure it, or take the value its seller publishes
the quiescent current of a dark pixel (i_idle_a): neither the product page nor this data sheet revision gives it – without it a dark strip draws nothing in the simulation
supply range only under 'Absolute Maximum Ratings' (+3.5 … +5.3 V); the electrical characteristics hold at 4.5–5.5 V
the product is discontinued (product page 2026-10-31); Pololu's SK6812 strips replace it, with 40 mA per LED and no published drop
